title: Smart Data Models - TM Forum Open APIs - PermissionSet
description: The PermissionSet is a set of Permissions granted to a user (party, party role or resource). The set may be granted explicitly by an authorized user or may be acquired implicitly due to the role that the user is playing. (TM Forum TMF672 User Role Permission Management API 5.1.0, OpenAPI component PermissionSet; attribute names kept verbatim except the NGSI-LD reserved terms / JSON-LD keywords renamed with a tmf prefix (id, @type, @baseType, @schemaLocation, ...); deprecated attributes left out.)

A PermissionSpecificationSet defines a set of permissions that can be attached to a party role specification. The resulting permissions will then apply to all users that adopt this party role. In TMF this is a PermissionSpecificationSetRef object; here the NGSI-LD id of the referenced PermissionSpecificationSet entity (urn:ngsi-ld:PermissionSpecificationSet:<tmf id>). Inline values and reference metadata (href, name, @referredType) are not kept.

AssetGroup.description: Defines a group of assets (entities) to which access can be controlled. Specific subclasses allow definition in various ways (list of entities, queries, ownership by customer, etc.). AssetGroup is not a managed entity, its concrete subclasses are always included by value in their containing entities.

allOf.description: Describes a given characteristic of an object or entity through a name/value pair. This is an abstract base class, the actual value is in one of the strongly-typed subclasses : StringCharacteristic, ObjectCharacteristic, FloatCharacteristic, BooleanCharacteristic, NumberCharacteristic, IntegerCharacteristic, StringArrayCharacteristic, ObjectArrayCharacteristic, BooleanArrayCharacteristic, NumberArrayCharacteristic, IntegerArrayCharacteristic... The value is given by the sub-class named in @type (discriminator in the TMF specification): NumberCharacteristic; see $defs.

valueType.description: Data type of the value of the characteristic

allOf.description: Another Characteristic that is related to the current Characteristic;
This class defines a characteristic specification.

name.description: A word, term, or phrase by which this characteristic specification is known and distinguished from other characteristic specifications.

valueType.description: A kind of value that the characteristic can take on, such as numeric, text and so forth

description.description: A narrative that explains the CharacteristicSpecification.

configurable.description: If true, the Boolean indicates that the target Characteristic is configurable

minCardinality.description: The minimum number of instances a CharacteristicValue can take on. For example, zero to five phone numbers in a group calling plan, where zero is the value for the minCardinality.

maxCardinality.description: The maximum number of instances a CharacteristicValue can take on. For example, zero to five phone numbers in a group calling plan, where five is the value for the maxCardinality.

isUnique.description: Specifies if the value of this characteristic is unique across all entities instantiated from the specification that uses this characteristic. For example, consider a ProductSpecification for a set-top box, with a CharacteristicSpecification cardID. Each set-top box must have a different value for cardID, so this isUnique attribute would be set to true for the characteristic.

regex.description: A rule or principle represented in regular expression used to derive the value of a characteristic value.

extensible.description: An indicator that specifies that the values for the characteristic can be extended by adding new values when instantiating a characteristic for a resource.

@valueSchemaLocation.description: This (optional) field provides a link to the schema describing the value type.

charSpecRelationship.description: An aggregation, migration, substitution, dependency or exclusivity relationship between/among Specification Characteristics.

characteristicValueSpecification.description: A CharacteristicValueSpecification object is used to define a set of attributes, each of which can be assigned to a corresponding set of attributes in a CharacteristicSpecification object. The values of the attributes in the CharacteristicValueSpecification object describe the values of the attributes that a corresponding Characteristic object can take on.

characteristicSpecificationId.description: Unique identifier of the characteristic within the specification

In general, a determinate quantity or magnitude of the kind designated, taken as a standard of comparison for others of the same kind, in assigning to them numerical values, as 1 foot, 1 yard, 1 mile, 1 square foot.

valueFrom.description: The low range value that a characteristic can take on

valueTo.description: The upper range value that a characteristic can take on

allOf.description: A characteristic which value is a Number.
Party role reference. A party role represents the part played by a party in a given context.

partyId.description: The identifier of the engaged party that is linked to the PartyRole object.

partyName.description: The name of the engaged party that is linked to the PartyRole object.

allOf.description: A Permission allows a user to carry out activities and/or access data in an entity. Permissions may apply globally (i.e. without reference to specific entities) or to an entity or set of entities.

characteristic.description: List of characteristics that apply to this permission, according to the corresponding specification

allOf.description: A PermissionSpecification defines a permissible action (e.g. read, write) on some function, where a function can be an entity class name or some specific functionality.

name.description: A descriptive name of the permission specification, should summarize to a human user what the purpose is of this permission

description.description: A fuller description of the permission specification, should describe to a human user what the purpose is of this permission
examples: User with this permission set can create and edit Product Offerings

function.description: The function to which the action applies, could be an entity class name, in which case the action defines permission to read or modify these entities. E.g. Read ProductOffering. Alternatively, the function is an agreed string that reflects a specific functionality to which access is controlled, such as giving an ad-hoc price reduction in a product order.

action.description: Level of access granted as part of the permission, such as read or write.

specificationCharacteristic.description: List of characteristics that are relevant for evaluating the permission. For example, if the permission relates to granting an ad-hoc order price reduction, a characteristic might be defined for the maximum allowed reduction.

PermissionSpecificationRef.description: A PermissionSpecificationRef defines a permissible action (e.g. read, write) on some function, where a function can be an entity class name or some specific functionality.

PermissionSpecificationRefOrValue.description: Related Entity reference. A related PermissionSpecification defines a PermissionSpecification described by reference or by value linked to a specific entity. The polymorphic attributes @type, @schemaLocation & @referredType are related to the PermissionSpecification entity and not the PermissionSpecificationRefOrValue class itself

PermissionSpecificationSetRef.description: A PermissionSpecificationSet defines a set of permissions that can be attached to a party role specification. The resulting permissions will then apply to all users that adopt this party role.

allOf.description: RelatedParty reference. A related party defines party or party role or its reference, linked to a specific entity

role.description: Role played by the related party or party role in the context of the specific entity it is linked to. Such as 'initiator', 'customer', 'salesAgent', 'user'

allOf.description: A RelatedSecurityPrincipal defines a SecurityPrincipal reference, linked to a specific entity

role.description: Role played by the related security principal in the context of the specific entity it is linked to.

ResourceRef.description: Resource reference, for when Resource is used by other entities.

SecurityPrincipalRef.description: A reference to a security principal.

TimePeriod.description: A period of time, either as a deadline (endDateTime only) a startDateTime only, or both

startDateTime.description: Start of the time period, using IETC-RFC-3339 format

endDateTime.description: End of the time period, using IETC-RFC-3339 format
